correctness.rationale: The all-positive-exponent inequality follows exactly from the product identity between nonzero roots and critical points and AM-GM. Equality forces unit-modulus nonzero roots and a common critical radius; combining the self-inversive coefficient relations of the root polynomial and the rescaled derivative leaves only endpoint coefficients and, in odd degree, the middle coefficient. The resulting quadratic-in-z^h criterion gives the stated sharp parameter interval. The radial stability bounds are direct consequences of the same product identity.

originality.rationale: The primary 2026 source already proves the stronger centered quadratic lower bound but does not classify its equality cases or state the all-lambda>0 centered refinement and stability theorem. Targeted literature and SCOPE-archive searches did not locate the parity-dependent equality family. Older equal-critical-radius results in the Smale mean-value literature are related but available statements address normalized critical values rather than this simultaneous root/critical-radius classification. Sheil-Small's full cited pages were not independently inspected and remain a residual risk; unindexed concurrent work is also possible.

value.rationale: The finding turns an endpoint estimate in the new Tang-Zhang work into a complete sharp theorem for every positive power, classifies all extremizers, reveals a parity bifurcation, and adds quantitative radial stability without claiming progress on the harder noncentral subquadratic problem.
